_scope_widened_after_the_claim_was_taken: DECLARED, NOT SLIPPED. The block-edit claim's purpose text says 'NETWORK 21 only' and the delivered change touches 21 AND 22. NETWORK 22 was the block's only set/reset mechanism (RCOIL DB_Input.Test[6]); C-403 is error severity and requires every S/R-written bit to appear in the startup-reset block, and OB100 does not name it. Converting it to the plain coil the rest of the contract already uses is behaviourally identical - while authoritative both write 0, while idle both leave this scan's value standing - and it removes an error-severity violation from a deployed block rather than leaving it beside a rewrite of the same resource. The claim is held by this agent and no other lane holds FB_HopperBlockageStim, so the widening collides with nobody; it is recorded here because a purpose text that understates the work is how scope drift starts.

_hand_written_line_count._why: NO GENERATOR EMITS THIS BLOCK. Harness.Map holds CopyLayerGenerator, SlotFcGenerator, StimShellGenerator, StimUdtGenerator, InstanceDbGenerator, CommsFbGenerator, CyclicObGenerator, LaneGenerator and ProgramGenerator, and not one emits an arbitration or injection-rest block. Reported as a generator gap rather than hand-written quietly. NOTE the gap got HARDER this pass, not easier: a generator can derive the index list mechanically, but the inert VALUE per index is a claim about the plant read off the consuming rung, so a generator would have to take it as declared input and refuse where it is undeclared.

Rewriting every release as a plain coil off AlwaysTrue satisfies the first clause, leaves no S/R mechanism to register, and removes the obligation instead of discharging it. header.commentBefore: Drives the three sensor signals the hopper-blockage monitor consumes - hopper high, plant running, operator reset - to a timeline the harness commands, so a conformance run exercises the monitor against a plant that behaves to order. A run is a clear-down that puts the monitor into a known unalarmed state, optionally a pre-boundary phase that leaves it part-way through its persistence window before the CPU is stopped and restarted, then the scenario itself, and once the harness has acknowledged the result by dropping the start bool, a trailing clear-down that repeats the reset so the NEXT run starts from a known unalarmed state rather than from whatever the previous scenario left standing - suppressed across a stop/restart boundary, where clearing would destroy the latched alarm the startup scenarios exist to observe. The clear-down exists because the monitor's alarm is latched and retentive and can only be cleared by a reset edge, so a scenario that did not start by clearing it would be reading the previous run. The scenario's shape comes from the tens digit of Profile and its durations from P1 to P4; six shapes cover every scenario the vector set asks for, because the scenarios differ in WHICH of the two driven signals drops and WHEN, never in anything else. The model publishes Armed so that observation latches are armed by its own phase - a latch running free from the start of the run would refill from the clear-down and read true no matter what the monitor did. It publishes its own threshold belief rather than reading the monitor's, so a reset placed at the threshold crossing stays a stimulus decision. This block drives the monitor's inputs and nothing else: it writes no plant tag, reads nothing the monitor writes, and is called only from the cyclic program.

networks.title: Force The Monitored Inputs
networks.beforeText:
NETWORK 21 "Force The Monitored Inputs"
  COMMENT "Presents the commanded plant to the input map through the input buffer's own test-injection members, which is the facility the input map already provides: with the test flag set the map ignores the physical terminal and takes each input from its test member. Only the flag and the two inputs this model commands are written, and only while a run is under way or the trailing clear-down after it is running - at every other time the flag is low and every input comes from the field exactly as it otherwise would. THE TRAILING CLEAR-DOWN IS WHY THE FLAG OUTLASTS THE RUN: its reset has to land on a hopper this model is still driving low, because a reset landing on a released input can be fighting the very cause it is trying to clear. The two commanded inputs need no such term - they are ANDed with the run, so outside a run they are already low, which is exactly the stopped plant and clear hopper the clear-down wants. The operator reset is written directly because it is not a field input and does not pass through the map."
  COIL DB_Input.Test[0] := Running OR InTrailingCleardown
  COIL DB_Input.Test[5] := Running AND Stim.Run
  COIL DB_Input.Test[8] := Running AND Stim.Hopper
  COIL DB_Controls.FaultReset := TrailingReset OR Running AND Stim.FaultReset
networks.afterText:
NETWORK 21 "Force The Monitored Inputs"
  COMMENT "Presents the commanded plant to the input map through the input buffer's own test-injection members: with the flag set the map takes each input from its test member instead of from the physical terminal. Every rung here passes through while this model is not driving, so a line this model does not own carries whatever head does own it, and the arbitration layer ahead of every head is what a pass-through rests on when no head owns a line at all. The flag itself is combined rather than owned - this model ORs itself in, and the flag is set whenever any head wants injection. The model stays authoritative through the trailing clear-down as well as the run, holding the two commanded inputs low there, so the clear-down's reset lands on a hopper this model is still driving low. The operator reset is written directly, being a control line rather than a field input that reaches the block through the map."
  COIL DB_Input.Test[0] := Running OR InTrailingCleardown OR DB_Input.Test[0]
  COIL DB_Input.Test[5] := Running AND Stim.Run OR NOT Running AND NOT InTrailingCleardown AND DB_Input.Test[5]
  COIL DB_Input.Test[8] := Running AND Stim.Hopper OR NOT Running AND NOT InTrailingCleardown AND DB_Input.Test[8]
  COIL DB_Controls.FaultReset := TrailingReset OR Running AND Stim.FaultReset OR NOT Running AND NOT InTrailingCleardown AND DB_Controls.FaultReset

networks.title: Hold The Reverse Feedback Clear
networks.beforeText:
NETWORK 22 "Hold The Reverse Feedback Clear"
  COMMENT "The model commands one running feedback, and the plant-running condition the monitor sees is the forward feedback or the reverse one. The reverse feedback's test member is therefore held clear for the whole run, and through the trailing clear-down that follows it, rather than left at whatever it happened to contain, so that the commanded stop is a stop and not merely the forward feedback going low. It extends across the clear-down for the same reason the injection flag does: a clear-down that let this member float could present a running plant to the monitor while the reset is trying to clear it."
  RCOIL DB_Input.Test[6] := Running OR InTrailingCleardown
networks.afterText:
NETWORK 22 "Hold The Reverse Feedback Clear"
  COMMENT "The plant-running condition the monitor sees is the forward feedback or the reverse one, and this model commands only the forward. The reverse feedback's test member is therefore held low for the whole run and through the trailing clear-down that follows it, so a commanded stop is a stop rather than the forward feedback alone going low. Outside those phases it passes through on the same contract as the network above."
  COIL DB_Input.Test[6] := NOT Running AND NOT InTrailingCleardown AND DB_Input.Test[6]

header.commentBefore: Owns the resting state of the two things every stimulus head shares, and owns nothing else: the input map's test-injection array, and the plant's single operator fault-reset line. It runs once, ahead of every head, and releases both, so a head finds on a line it does not own either that line's released value or what another head wrote in this same scan. THE RELEASED VALUE IS THE INERT VALUE FOR WHOEVER READS THAT INDEX, which is not the same thing as zero: an index whose reader treats HIGH as its quiet state is released HIGH, because a zero there asserts a stop or a motion demand of its own. Each released value is taken from the block that consumes the index; an index no block reads is released low and said here to be undetermined. Heads keep their own writes. While a head is not authoritative it passes a line through unchanged, and this release is what that pass-through rests on, so a head added later needs one rung per index and no knowledge of its neighbours. The operator fault-reset line belongs to the harness while this program is loaded: it is released every scan, so a press at an operator station does not reach the control. That suits a bench rig with no operator station and suits nothing else.

_c103_disposition: WITHDRAWN, NOT DEFENDED. The first hand-back justified 24 C-103 warnings as the documented cross-block set/reset exception. A blind review refuted that on four grounds and it is not carried forward: nothing SETs those bits (every head write is a plain assign, and no SCOIL on any of them exists in the project), the ruling's direction is set-outside/reset-inside-a-reusable-FB and this was the reverse, the ruling's safety rests on each setter touching only its own instance while this is one FC reaching into a global DB three FBs contend for, and the tool's own message scopes itself to the reusable-FB pattern. The disposition is not 'accept the warning' either. Rewriting the releases as plain coils removed every reset coil from the block, so there is now nothing for C-103 to report: preflight and review are both clean at zero findings. The same rewrite removed the block's C-403 exposure at the root, and removed the one pre-existing C-103 in FB_HopperBlockageStim NETWORK 22.
_c308_disposition: DB_Controls.FaultReset has four writers and that is acceptable, but NOT because a reset pairs with an assign - doc 06 sanctions no such pairing, and after this pass there is no reset among them anyway. The justification is ORDERING: the four writers are totally ordered by OB1 network order (arbiter 1, hopper 2, pusher 3, shredder 4), each later writer's expression carries the previous value as a pass-through term so no write is lost, and the sole consumer FC_ControlMain runs after all four. THAT IS WHAT STOPS BEING TRUE IF OB1 IS REORDERED, which is why it is recorded here and stated in the block's own NETWORK 4 comment rather than left as a property a reader has to rediscover.

_deferred_review_findings.finding: F-4 (C-607) / F-6 (one-reading): `Running OR InTrailingCleardown` appears unnamed four times in FB_HopperBlockageStim, and the head's guard `NOT Running AND NOT InTrailingCleardown` diverges from the other two heads' `NOT Running`.
_deferred_review_findings.why: The suggested repair is a named Static (`Authoritative`). Adding a static to FB_HopperBlockageStim is an INTERFACE change: it routes to gen-block-modify-purpose rather than the fix path, it resizes iDB_HopperBlockageStim, and it forces --allow-header on the invariance gate - the exact profile this run was scoped to avoid on a deployed block. Worth recording about the divergence itself: it is not two spellings of one contract. This head's authority window genuinely is wider than the other two, because it keeps driving through its trailing clear-down, so collapsing the guards to match would be wrong. What is left is the readability point, and that is real.

_deferred_review_findings.finding: F-5 (C-602): FB_HopperBlockageStim NETWORK 21's fault-reset rung is 3 OR-branches and 6 contacts, over the guide, with no applicable exception.
_deferred_review_findings.why: It is the same fix as F-4/F-6 - the named static is what shortens it - and carries the same interface-change routing.

_new_defect_found_not_fixed.class: the same one this block was built for - a shared harness-written line with no rest owner
_new_defect_found_not_fixed.traced: PusherMode is written only by MOVEs gated on a head's Running (pusher head NETWORK 20, shredder head NETWORK 26), so while no head runs it is a self-hold carrying the last value written. It is NOT part of the injection array and this arbiter does not release it. The path that makes it matter opened this pass: releasing Test[1] and Test[15] high clears the sequencer's stop-all, which clears PusherCycleInhibitCmd, and releasing Test[12] high satisfies the pusher's LaunchRequest term `IO.HomeLimit`. With HopperHighLevel driven high by a hopper scenario, the only remaining term holding a pusher cycle off during a hopper index is IO.Mode being 0 - which is to say, PusherMode's residue.
_new_defect_found_not_fixed.currently_masked_by: The pusher head writes CmdMode 0 whenever it is Running and not InScenario, so the last value it leaves behind is 0. That is a property of one head's cleardown, not a guarantee of the layer.
_new_defect_found_not_fixed.proposed_fix: MOVE(EN := TRUE, IN := 0) => DB_Controls.PusherMode, in this block, alongside the reset-line release.
_new_defect_found_not_fixed.why_not_done: ASKING FOR A ROUTING DECISION RATHER THAN DEFERRING QUIETLY. It is outside the two resources this block was chartered and claimed for, it is the operator command surface rather than the injection layer, and the shredder head holds PusherMode at 0 for its whole index as a DECLARED plant assumption tied to an excluded-signal declaration in its binding - so changing who owns its rest state interacts with another lane's declared binding and should be decided by someone who can see both. One line to overrule.

_behaviour_change_to_the_deployed_hba_sl.retraction: THE FIRST HAND-BACK'S CLAIM WAS STRONGER THAN WHAT NOW HOLDS AND IS WITHDRAWN. It said the deployed slot was bit-identical everywhere. With per-index inert release that is no longer true: Test[1], Test[12] and Test[15] now read HIGH during a hopper index where the deployed program has them at 0.
_behaviour_change_to_the_deployed_hba_sl.correction_absorbed: The first argument was also necessary but not sufficient. The load-bearing fact, which the review supplied, is that Test[1] and Test[11..15] were ALREADY 0 in the deployed baseline - nothing wrote them and OB100 does not touch DB_Input.Test[] - so the pass-through repair changed nothing only because of that, not because of the pass-through form itself.
_behaviour_change_to_the_deployed_hba_sl.what_is_unchanged: The slot's OBSERVED set, traced end to end. FB_HopperBlockageMonitor reads HopperLevelHigh (Test[8]), PlantRunning (Test[5] OR Test[6]) and FaultReset - all four owned by the hopper head itself. FB_HarnessViolationLatch reads only iDB_HopperBlockageStim.Stim.* and iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.IO.*. None of Test[1], Test[12] or Test[15] reaches either by any path.
_behaviour_change_to_the_deployed_hba_sl.what_changes: The plant around the slot. The sequencer's stop-all condition goes from asserted, via the absent healthy and downstream contacts, to clear; the pusher reads a parked ram instead of one away from home. On the currently deployed program neither can act: the sequencer needs a CycleStart press and Test[3] releases low, so Step stays 0, and PusherMode is 0 because the pusher head is not loaded. On the three-head program the residual dependency is PusherMode - see _new_defect_found_not_fixed.
_behaviour_change_to_the_deployed_hba_sl.verdict: No observable change to the 23 vectors is predicted, and that prediction is a STATIC trace, not a wave. It has not been run, and this is the claim most worth re-testing on the first wave after deployment.
